name: Taco Azul, INC
notes: First-party ordering data pulled directly from the restaurant's own WordPress site via its Clover ordering plugin's REST API (moo-clover), address confirmed exact (14110 Olde Hwy 80 Suite C, El Cajon 92021, phone (619) 486-6768 matches homepage contact block). 24 categories fetched, 163 priced items total. Prices are plain integers in cents (e.g. "1139" = $11.39), converted directly with no scaling/division applied. Cent-ending distribution is dominated by .99 (107/163) with a long tail of conventional endings (.49/.95/.00/.50/etc) -- typical genuine US menu pricing, not a markup signature (no single divisor concentrates prices onto round values). A few catering bulk-pack items ($120-$315 for 10-30 person trays, 50-200 piece taco packs) and one $0.36 side salsa were manually checked and are legitimate, not corrupted fields. Site's About-section boilerplate text is generic templated filler mentioning 'Whitestone, New York' but the concrete contact block (address/phone/hours) matches the batch record exactly, so this is a site-content-quality oddity, not a wrong-location signal.

name: Junior's Taco Shop
notes: No website in the work list. Address confirmed exact via Uber Eats store page (1680 S Melrose Dr, Vista 92084, batch record says Ste 110). Payload used the client-fetched catalogSectionsMap/catalogItems shape (no schema.org JSON-LD) -- required a fix beyond the documented %5C" / \" unescape order: a nested 'metaJson' field (FAQPage schema junk) contained literal 3-char '%5C' sequences that were never actually converted to real backslashes before the outer JSON was assembled, so embedded quotes inside it terminated the JSON string early. Decoded '%5C' -> '\\' globally first, then the standard escape rules parsed cleanly. 109 priced items across 15 sections (Breakfast Plates, Tacos, Burritos, Combination Plates, etc). Ran a full divisor sweep (1.00-1.35) for a delivery-markup signature -- no divisor above 1.00 beat the baseline 45.9% round-number rate, so there is no evidence of a baked-in markup; treating these Uber Eats prices as close to first-party. Flag: Yelp's 'Popular Dishes' snippet lists a few items ~30% higher (Carne Asada Taco $4.60 on Yelp vs $3.40 here) but that Yelp menu is marked 'prices as of July 28, 2024' (stale, 2 years old) and is Yelp's own scraped/crowd data, not treated as more authoritative than the current first-party ordering feed.

name: Black Plague Purgatory Lounge
notes: NOT_FOUND: independent source (The Coast News, a North County San Diego local news outlet -- not the venue's own site) reports, in an article dated October 1, 2025: 'Black Plague Brewing permanently closed its Oceanside and Escondido locations over the weekend... Black Plague officially shuttered its Oceanside and Escondido sites on Sept. 28.' The Escondido location named in the article is explicitly the Purgatory Lounge (239 E Valley Pkwy, matches the batch address), a taproom that partnered with Full Metal Burgers for food service. The brewery's own site (blackplaguebrewing.com) is still live and its homepage doesn't mention the closure, but the independent news report is dated, specific, and unambiguous about permanence, satisfying the bar for not_found rather than blocked.
